record_text: Change approval record. Change Policy CP-7, section 3 allows a production data-store upgrade when a rollback rehearsal passes and post-upgrade headroom is at least 25%. For change request CR-2291 the rollback rehearsal on 4 March passed (test report TR-118) and the 5 March capacity review measured 38% headroom. The Change Advisory Board approved CR-2291 on 6 March under that section.

Retention exception record. The records manager approved keeping the Riverside design files until 2031 on 16 January because asset register entry AR-5520 shows the bridge in its inspection programme until then. The approval also states that all other Riverside project records carry no ongoing value and can be destroyed now.

Procurement award record. Tender T-0417 was published on 1 April and closed on 14 April with four compliant bids. The panel scored the bids on 18 April (score sheet SS-4417), with Northline Print highest at 82 of 100. The award to Northline Print was issued on 22 April, and the standstill period ended on 2 May.

Records request determination. Request RQ-0912 for the 2025 facilities maintenance contracts was partly refused on 3 June under section 6 of the Information Access Policy. Section 6 covers commercially confidential material. The requester was told of the refusal in writing.

Change approval record. Change request CR-2291, the reporting database upgrade, was approved on 6 March. The board approved it because the change met the standard for approval. Since the upgrade was judged acceptable, approval was the appropriate outcome, and the minutes record that the change was approved.

Records request determination. Request RQ-0912 was partly refused on 3 June. Two contracts were withheld because they were not suitable for release. They were not suitable for release because the records team decided to withhold them, and the partial refusal follows from that decision.

Change approval record. Two changes were considered on 6 March. Change request CR-2291, the reporting database upgrade, was approved because its rollback rehearsal passed (test report TR-118). Change request CR-2294, a firewall rule change, was declined because its rollback plan had not been tested and no test report was submitted. Each outcome is recorded under its own minutes item (items 3 and 4).

Retention exception record. The Riverside design files will be kept until 2031, three years past the schedule, because the bridge remains in its 10-year inspection programme (asset register entry AR-5520) and inspection report IR-77 of 9 January relies on the files. The records manager approved the exception on 16 January.

Procurement award record. Tender T-0417 was awarded to Northline Print on 22 April because its bid scored highest at 82 of 100 (score sheet SS-4417, dated 18 April). The panel further concluded that Northline Print will meet every delivery target over the contract term and that delivery monitoring can be dropped.

Retention exception record. The project team asked on 12 January to keep the Riverside design files for 3 years beyond the 7-year schedule. The asset register shows the bridge is still under its 10-year inspection programme (entry AR-5520), and inspection report IR-77 of 9 January cites the design files twice. The records manager approved the exception on 16 January; the approval cites entry AR-5520 and report IR-77.

Procurement award record. Procurement Rule 4.2 requires award to the compliant bid with the highest total score on the published criteria. For tender T-0417, panel score sheet SS-4417 dated 18 April gives Northline Print 82 of 100, the highest of the four compliant bids. The contract was awarded to Northline Print on 22 April under Rule 4.2.
